newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call money slips as banks square positions.
newsitem.headline: Manila call money slips as banks square positions.

text.p: * Average interbank call rate softens to 11.09275 pct
The Philippine overnight rate softened to 11.09375 percent from Thursday's 11.625 percent as major banks had squared their positions, traders said.
"It's the end of the reserve week. Most of the borrowing banks in the past days have already squared their positions," a trader said.
Turnover reached 18.635 billion pesos with 36 lenders out of 57 institutions who participated in the market.
Done rates ranged from a low of 11.03125 percent to a high of 11.75 percent.
He said the maturing special series and regular Treasury bills have also contributed to the liquidity in the market. He estimated that about 20 billion pesos have been freed up in the past days.
The secondary market was active with sellers dominating the market, since banks expected the rates to firm up in the coming weeks.
Effective yields of Treasury bills in the secondary market nudged higher than last week's auction rates.
The three-month bills were being sold at 11.5 percent, six-month bills at 11.85 percent, while the one-year bills at 12.6 to 12.65 percent.
